content.user_title: Create Consistent Pixel Art with Layer
content.value_statement: Generated pixel art can have blurred edges, inconsistent palettes, and mismatched animation frames. This skill guides Layer workflows using explicit grids, approved references, and sprite sheet tools.
actual_capabilities: Guide prompts with numeric sprite dimensions, palette counts, color families, and visual eras.
Specify hard edges, transparent backgrounds, and exclusions for blur, gradients, and anti-aliasing.
Plan separate animation frames using one approved reference to reduce character drift.
Guide consistent trained-style references and compatible model selection across animation frames.
Direct Layer sprite sheet packing and splitting through the tools' declared schemas.
Route seamless pixel tile requests toward tileability-capable models and texture guidance.
limitations: Requires access to Layer generation and sprite sheet tools; this skill contains guidance, not their implementations.
General generation mechanics and detailed tiling guidance depend on sibling skills.
Generated results still require review; exact pixel grids and frame consistency are not guaranteed.
Does not provide engine integration, animation playback, or a local pixel editing application.

use_cases.title: Build a Character Walk Cycle
use_cases.description: Generate an approved contact pose, create three matching poses, review consistency, and assemble a transparent sprite sheet.

use_cases.title: Prepare Consistent Pixel Icons
use_cases.description: Specify dimensions, palette, visual era, and background requirements for a coordinated set of pixel icons.

use_cases.title: Revise an Existing Sprite Frame
use_cases.description: Split a sprite sheet into cells, edit the selected frame, and repack the frames after reviewing alignment.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Sprite
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 32x32 pixel art knight with a 16-color palette and transparent background. Exclude blur, gradients, soft shadows, and anti-aliasing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: generate one clearly specified sprite.

prompt_templates.title: Review Pixel Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this sprite for blurred edges, anti-aliasing, grid mismatch, and palette drift. Suggest revised Layer prompt constraints before generating a replacement.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: diagnose common pixel art defects.

prompt_templates.title: Assemble a Walk Cycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a four-frame 32x32 walk cycle from my approved contact pose. Reference that pose for every frame, review consistency, then pack the sheet.

prompt_templates.title: Apply a Trained Pixel Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my trained pixel style for a four-frame cycle. Keep reference sets, weight, palette, and approved frame constant; omit base_model_id and inspect tool schemas.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: maintain trained-style settings across frame generation.

output_examples.input: Prepare a 32x32 knight sprite with a limited palette.
output: Sprite specification: 32x32 grid, 16 colors, side view, and 16-bit shading.
Generation constraints: transparent background, hard edges, no blur, no gradients, and no anti-aliasing.
Review criteria: palette consistency, clear silhouette, and clean pixel boundaries.

output_examples.input: Plan a four-frame walk cycle from my approved sprite.
output: Frame sequence: contact, down, passing, and up.
Reference plan: attach the approved contact frame to every remaining generation.
Consistency review: compare height, palette, and armor details; regenerate mismatched frames.
Assembly plan: pack the approved frames into uniform cells on a transparent sprite sheet.

output_examples.input: Edit one frame from an existing sprite sheet.
output: Split the sheet into individual cells in reading order.
Revise the selected frame while preserving the original grid and palette.
Review the revised frame alongside unchanged frames before repacking.

best_practices: Specify numeric grid dimensions, palette size, color family, visual era, and background before generating.
Approve one reference frame and reuse it for every remaining animation pose.
Read tool schemas, review frames together, and regenerate inconsistent frames before packing.
anti_patterns: Requesting an entire sprite sheet in one image generation.
Chaining each animation frame from the previous frame instead of the approved first frame.
Omitting pixel dimensions and hard-edge exclusions, then relying on downsampling to repair the result.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Actual generation requires access to the relevant Layer tools.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and uses external Layer tools for image generation, sprite packing, and sprite splitting.

faq.question: Can it guarantee a perfect 32x32 sprite?
faq.answer: No. Explicit dimensions and exclusions guide generation, but you must inspect the output for grid accuracy and clean edges.

faq.question: How does it keep animation frames consistent?
faq.answer: Every new frame references the approved first frame. The workflow also keeps palette and style settings consistent and reviews frames together.

faq.question: Can it split an existing sprite sheet?
faq.answer: It directs Layer's split_sprite_sheet tool to cut cells in reading order. You must consult the tool schema for required arguments.

faq.question: What happens when a sibling skill is missing?
faq.answer: It asks the user to install the missing sibling skill. In unattended workflows, it proceeds from available tool schemas and flags the gap.
